Normal review — completed before the separate skill passes.

No actionable production-code defect found in the reviewed change.

Reviewed `80bce9a08d682677f970505eb0f314538a3f4aa8` against `0ee8671d355863658bbf292a12e04a566ac1af29` (`jhan-vnnik-2-amx`).

- Reviewed the nine-file diff, the block transpose and masks, source conversion, cache accessors, generated calls, and relevant callers.
- Traced source-row readiness, publication of shared work, helper completion, and the main thread's completion marks and downstream notifications. [Save implementation](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/blob/80bce9a08d682677f970505eb0f314538a3f4aa8/h/tron/models/model.hpp#L3303)
- Inspected the generated Qwen3 plugin from the build at this commit. Its main call follows the per-token K-channel waits. Its helper call follows the K-producing kernel.
- Checked the recorded feature-on, feature-off and AMX-dispatch-off test results at this commit. AMX means Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. The disabled-dispatch numerics cases are placeholders. The kill-switch run skips the AMX-specific cases.

`git diff --check` passed during this review. I did not rerun product tests or benchmarks. The recorded host suite has 93 passes, one unidentified skip, and the documented `t_proxy_llama31` failure caused by the missing Python environment. The separate skill passes follow.

Separate pass: `tron-code-review`.

One coverage finding is attached to the shared-save test: its external thread joins hide whether the production call itself waited for all helpers.

Reviewed `80bce9a08d682677f970505eb0f314538a3f4aa8` against `0ee8671d355863658bbf292a12e04a566ac1af29` (`jhan-vnnik-2-amx`).

Checked the packed and row-major paths, one-token and partial/full-block stores, mixed KV-write flags, worker-count limits, repeated windows, and generated operations that share a slot without writing it. KV means stored attention keys and values. The AMX kill switch does not change the store's layout or sharing decision. I also traced the fresh batch lifetime and the main-only completion marks, dispatch credits and downstream notifications.

The existing records include two mutation checks and feature-on/off runs at this commit. Neither mutation removes the production completion wait. No new product test, mutation run, or hardware workload was executed during this pass. The accepted CI exception tracked by #4865 remains separate from this finding.

Separate pass: `wade-code-review`.

Short version: one non-blocking description finding from checks 6 and 8. Nine throughput decision bands use rounded inputs. None of the comparison classifications changes.

Reviewed `80bce9a08d682677f970505eb0f314538a3f4aa8` against `0ee8671d355863658bbf292a12e04a566ac1af29` (`jhan-vnnik-2-amx`).

**[P3] Calculate the band from unrounded standard deviations, then format it.**

Measurements defines the band as twice the larger sample standard deviation, with a minimum of 0.4 TPS. TPS means tokens per second per user. The body-generation script reads the rounded values from `summary.md` before multiplying them. The full-precision values remain in the recorded `pr3-E-cpu/summary.json` repetitions.

For example, the parent binary's standard deviation in the 2-device, 1,024-token cell is 0.4352492521 TPS. Twice that is 0.8704985042 TPS, displayed as **0.87 TPS**. Rounding the standard deviation to 0.44 TPS first produces the posted **0.88 TPS**.

| Cell | Comparison | Posted band | Band from full-precision data |
|---|---|---|---|
| tp2, prompt 1024 tokens | new vs head | 0.88 TPS | 0.87 TPS |
| tp2, prompt 1024 tokens | newoff vs new | 0.44 TPS | 0.43 TPS |
| tp2, prompt 1024 tokens | newoff vs headoff | 0.76 TPS | 0.77 TPS |
| tp2, prompt 1024 tokens | head vs base | 0.88 TPS | 0.87 TPS |
| tp4, prompt 1024 tokens | new vs base | 0.96 TPS | 0.95 TPS |
| tp4, prompt 1024 tokens | new vs head | 1.26 TPS | 1.25 TPS |
| tp4, prompt 1024 tokens | newoff vs new | 0.72 TPS | 0.71 TPS |
| tp4, prompt 1024 tokens | newoff vs headoff | 1.34 TPS | 1.33 TPS |
| tp4, prompt 1024 tokens | head vs base | 1.26 TPS | 1.25 TPS |

Please calculate from `summary.json` or the raw repetitions, and update the repeated band values in the prose. `tp2` and `tp4` mean 2 and 4 devices. The time-to-first-token bands do not need this correction.

I independently recomputed all 15 measurement rows and all 15 paired comparisons from the recorded repetitions. Their means, standard deviations, paired t statistics and inside/beyond classifications agree with the description. This finding concerns the displayed bands only.

The other check categories produced no additional source finding. The three commits are topical. The option gates and draft CI filtering match the workflow/configuration files. The current draft has no required checks reported by `gh pr checks --required`; its product jobs are skipped, while the reported lint, infrastructure and Debian smoke checks passed. No source test or sanitizer run was added during this pass. The test-completion finding is recorded once in the preceding `tron-code-review` pass.

Separate pass: `ben-review`.

No actionable abstraction or interface finding.

Reviewed `80bce9a08d682677f970505eb0f314538a3f4aa8` against `0ee8671d355863658bbf292a12e04a566ac1af29` (`jhan-vnnik-2-amx`).

I inspected the five-argument `set_k_block`, `store_k_block`, `save_k_impl`, and runtime `save_k` interfaces, including their callers and existing row-view helpers. Their arguments carry distinct selections or execution context. The worker index/count pair follows the generated kernels' existing convention. The mask and row-pointer array have one production construction site, so their presence does not establish a repeated abstraction problem.

Packed-address arithmetic stays in the tensor operation. The page accessor forwards a typed plane view. The existing source/destination row helpers are reused for the conversion paths. This pass was an interface review; it made no source changes and ran no product tests.

Separate pass: `plain-english`, Check mode, on the current PR description. Short version: 16 passages need terminology, sentence or paragraph edits. The first two summary sentences contain 88 and 123 whitespace-delimited words. A three-sentence limit does not require putting all implementation details and comparisons in those sentences. Rule occurrence counts (a passage can violate several rules): rule 1: 3, rule 2: 9, rule 5: 1, rule 6: 1, rule 7: 6, rule 8: 5. Rule 1 defines terms, rule 2 separates claims, rule 5 requires a short summary, rule 6 uses literal wording, rule 7 separates points, and rule 8 prefers short sentences. The replacements retain the detailed measurements and limitations elsewhere in the description. The full proposed description is supplied separately as a collapsed comment. It also includes the numeric-band correction from the Wade pass. The live description has not been edited.

Three cases store on the calling thread alone:

- A pass has at most 16 tokens, such as a decode step in the 8-user runs.
- The caller passes one worker. This covers the handwritten plugins and the unit tests, except the three-thread section of `t_llama_unit` (the model and cache unit-test binary).
- The caller passes more than 128 workers. | | 7, 8 | **The changes: window fields**: - `batch::k_store_window_t` holds the claim counter `next_unit` on its own cache line (a claim must not invalidate the line the waiting threads poll), the counters `opened` and `finished`, the unit count, the unit table of `max_minibatch_size + 1` entries, and `helper_windows`, one counter per helper of the windows it has entered. The size of that array, 128, bounds the worker count of a shared store. One window state exists per minibatch. It holds the claim counter on its own 64-byte cache line, the counters `opened` and `finished` and the unit count (12 bytes), the unit table (4 bytes per entry, `max_minibatch_size + 1` entries) and the 512-byte `helper_windows` array. With the generated plugins' `max_minibatch_size` of 1,024 that is 4,736 bytes, alignment padding included. | One `batch::k_store_window_t` exists per minibatch. Its fields are:

\| Field \| Purpose and size \|
\|---\|---\|
\| `next_unit` \| Assigns work units. It occupies its own 64-byte cache line, so claims do not invalidate the line that waiting threads poll. \|
\| `opened`, `finished`, `n_units` \| Count opened windows, finished helpers and work units. Together they occupy 12 bytes. \|
\| `unit_start` \| The unit table: `max_minibatch_size + 1` entries, at 4 bytes per entry. \|
\| `helper_windows` \| Each helper's entered-window count. The array has 128 entries and occupies 512 bytes. Its capacity bounds the shared worker count. \|

The generated plugins allow 1,024 items per minibatch. Their window state occupies 4,736 bytes, including alignment padding. | | 2, 7, 8 | **The changes: shared-save protocol**: - `save_k_impl` takes the worker index and the worker count. An unshared store is the main thread's alone: a helper returns at once. In a shared store the main thread cuts the units, resets the claim counter and `finished` to 0, and increments `opened` with release ordering. Release and acquire are the C++ memory orders of atomic operations: every write a thread makes before its release increment is visible to the thread whose acquire read sees that increment. A helper's W-th shared call waits until `opened` reaches W with acquire ordering, so window W of a pass is the W-th shared `save_k` of that pass on both sides. Every thread claims units with an atomic add on the claim counter and stores each unit it claims. A helper increments `finished` with release ordering when its claim loop ends and returns. The main thread waits until `finished` equals `n_workers - 1` with acquire ordering. Every row store therefore happens before the main thread continues. The watchdog runs inside that wait. | `save_k_impl` takes the worker index and worker count. For an unshared store, helpers return immediately. For a shared store, the sequence is:

1. The main thread creates the work units and resets `next_unit` and `finished` to zero.
2. It increments `opened` with release ordering.
3. Each helper waits for its W-th shared window with an acquire read of `opened`.
4. Every worker claims unit indices with an atomic add. It stores each unit it claims.
5. Each helper increments `finished` with release ordering after its claim loop ends. It then returns.
6. The main thread waits for all `n_workers - 1` helpers with acquire reads of `finished`. The watchdog checks this wait.

Release and acquire are C++ memory orders for atomic operations. Writes made before a release become visible through the corresponding acquire. The main thread therefore observes every helper's row stores before it continues. The W-th shared call on each helper matches the W-th window opened by main. | | 2, 8 | **The changes: QK orientation**: Note [QK orientation] in the kernel interface names the K store, with its two store paths, and the reader as the two places the extra work of the flipped orientation moves to (the kernel takes the query rows as the left operand of the tile multiply and the packed K plane as the right operand, the reverse of `main`'s row-major AMX kernel).
